```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
base_dir <- "./canopy_photos/raw_hemisphere_images"   # top-level folder

# Find all image files recursively
files <- list.files(
  base_dir,
  pattern = "\\.(jpg|jpeg|png|tif|tiff|dng)$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

for(f in files) {

  # Folder containing the image
  site_name <- basename(dirname(f))

  # Current filename
  old_name <- basename(f)

  # Skip if already prefixed
  if(startsWith(old_name, paste0(site_name, "_"))) next

  # New filename
  new_name <- paste0(site_name, "_", old_name)

  file.rename(
    from = f,
    to   = file.path(dirname(f), new_name)
  )

  cat(old_name, "->", new_name, "\n")
}
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
